A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoCoA–ADMM study. Their text, equations, four figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–D are available and readable, supporting a complete comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original parameter-sensitivity experiments, synthetic ridge/lasso regression results, and real-data SVM experiments in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 6, Figures 2–4, and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) retain the same Consensus-PD, LinConsensus-PD, Proximal-1-PD, Proximal-2-PD, and CoCoA-PD updates. Expanded proof explanations and solver-accuracy guidance do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic ridge/lasso regression with the same IID and non-IID generators, and ridge/lasso SVMs on a1a, w8a, and real-sim. Section 6 and Appendix D introduce no additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The three-method parameter-sensitivity comparison is unchanged. Ridge experiments retain CoCoA-PD and the four ADMM variants, while lasso experiments retain the four ADMM variants. Newly cited methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1's sample, feature, and machine counts remain unchanged, as do the 500-round a1a tuning experiment, regularization settings, gap metric, and synthetic n=3000, d=500, K=30 setup. The new inner-solver guidance is not reported as an experimental protocol revision.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the same parameter-sensitivity questions and evidence, and Figure 3 retains the same IID/non-IID comparisons. No new ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study appears in the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version discloses repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice for the retained curves is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 contain identical embedded result graphics, including the plotted curves and numerical axes. Table 1 and the associated empirical findings are unchanged, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes P from positive semidefinite to positive definite. New Remark 1 supplies Schur-complement/rank conditions and excludes rank-deficient cases; Section 5 also adds assumptions to the iterate-convergence assertion, and Appendix B.1 adds a convergence argument. These changes substantially revise theoretical applicability while retaining the bounds. Remark 1's P1 condition conflicts with Lemma 2.

C1.justification: The revised abstract explicitly limits CoCoA coincidence to ridge-regularized dual updates and qualifies consensus/proximal equivalence by a sign reversal. These qualifications already appeared in v2's body; v3 also drops the introductory encoder/privacy contribution language. The central unification and tuning claims and the conclusion remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds applicability limits for rank-deficient data blocks and explains why logistic-loss conjugates may require more inner iterations and why machine precision limits useful refinement. Interpretations of the retained experimental results are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6 replaces the generic supplementary-material code reference with an explicit Google Drive link. Section 5 adds accuracy guidance, including a 1/t² residual target and logarithmic inner-iteration growth under linear convergence. Hardware disclosures and Appendix D's data-generation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds focused positioning against earlier unification work, citing Esser et al. (2010), Shefi and Teboulle (2014), and Beck (2017). Smith et al. (2015) and He et al. (2018) are also added; Shalev-Shwartz and Zhang (2013) is removed. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, replacing the numbered contribution list with a narrative on earlier unification work and practical implications. The title, author block, and citation style change, and Appendix B.5 explains the existing time-index shift more fully.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the TMLR template throughout, changing typography, headers, front matter, and page composition. Figure 1 is redrawn in monochrome and moved into the introduction. Tables, plots, and appendices are reflowed, while Figures 2–4 preserve their empirical graphics.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies claim scope, prior-work context, proof explanations, and code access, but introduces an error in the convergence-applicability discussion: Remark 1 states K^{-1}B ≻ AᵀA for P1, whereas the Schur complement of Lemma 2's matrix requires KB ≻ AᵀA. The explanatory gains coexist with this defect in a central theoretical discussion, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
